rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ignorant are those who know but do not act; one who sins this way is no better than an ignorant person.
rows.anchor: الذين لا يعملون بما يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ignorance means foolishness: the wise person would not commit the indecent act urged on Joseph; adultery belongs to foolish conduct.
rows.anchor: أو من السفهاء بارتكاب ما يدعونني إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever commits adultery has entered the ranks of lying ignoramuses.
rows.anchor: وإن من زنى فقد دخل من جملة الكاذبين في الجهال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s prayer asked God to turn away the women’s plot; the verb may govern the prayer directly or govern the supplicant with li, leaving ‘prayer’ implicit.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه استدعاء لصرف كيدهن والاستجابة تتعدى إلى الدعاء بنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turned away their plot as Joseph asked and made him steadfast in chastity, so he accepted prison and hardship over pleasure entailing sin.
rows.anchor: فصرف عنه كيدهن حسب دعائه وثبته على العصمة والعفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the prayers of the distressed and knows their circumstances and what benefits them.
rows.anchor: السميع لدعاء المتضرعين إليه العليم بأحوالهم وما يصلحهم

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو بكر الدقاق
rows.claim: After resisting desire for milk and a beautiful woman, al-Daqqaq dreamt Joseph praised his escape from that temptation and recited that whoever fears God’s standing receives two gardens.
rows.anchor: وعن الشيخ أبي بكر الدقاق قدس سره قال : بقيت بمكة

rows.speaker: منشدون
rows.claim: The cited couplet warns that letting the gaze roam exhausts the heart with sights it cannot attain or patiently forgo.
rows.anchor: وأنت إذا أرسلت طرفك رائدا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A person cannot escape the self by relying on the self; escape is possible only through God.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : لا يمكن الخروج من النفس بالنفس

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو تراب النخشبي
rows.claim: Turning someone already occupied with God away from God brings immediate divine displeasure; nothing equals protection from sin.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ أبو تراب النخشبي قدس سره : من شغل مشغولا بالله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The heart is held in the prison of religious law and divine protection when it refuses worldly and lower-self prompting; even a prophet’s heart would incline without God’s protection.
rows.anchor: والقلب وإن كان في كمالية قلب نبي من الأنبياء لو خلي وطبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then it appeared’ signals that the Aziz and his advisers changed their view about Joseph.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر للعزيز وأصحابه المتصدين للحل والعقد رأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs they saw included the infant’s testimony and the torn shirt, among other evidence of Joseph’s innocence.
rows.anchor: الشواهد على براءة يوسف كشهادة الصبي وقد القميص وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers’ stated aim was to silence public talk; the woman instead intended prison to humble Joseph and make people think him guilty.
rows.anchor: أي إلى حين انقطاع قالة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accounts give the imprisonment as five, seven, or, more famously, twelve years; Ibn al-Shaykh says the verse fixes no duration, only a long stay.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ لا دلالة في الآية على تعيين مدة حبسه وإنما القدر المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A period is linguistically indefinite and can be short or long; in juristic oaths an unqualified ‘while’ means six months unless a specific time was intended.
rows.anchor: والحين عند أهل اللغة وقت من الزمان غير محدود ويقع على القصير منه والطويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The act of imprisonment is omitted and supplied by the next verse; the Aziz knew Joseph’s innocence, so the woman devised another tactic and accused him of disgracing her.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية محذوف والتقدير لما تغير رأيهم في حقه ورأوا حبسه حبسوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two youths were the king’s cupbearer and baker; they were jailed after a poisoning plot, which the cupbearer abandoned but the baker carried out.
rows.anchor: من عبيد الملك الأكبر وهو ريان بن الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer dreamt of three grape clusters, squeezed them into the king’s cup, and served him; wine names the grapes by what they become.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة أغصان عليها ثلاثة عناقيد من عنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The baker dreamt he carried bread above his head; above means on, as in the command to strike above the necks.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخر وهو الخباز إني أريني كأني في مطبخ الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The baker’s dream had three baskets of bread and foods, with birds of prey eating from the upper basket.
rows.anchor: فوق رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها خبز وألوان الأطعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differ on whether the prisoners truly dreamt or feigned dreams to test Joseph; the rescued cupbearer spoke truth, while the other lied and was crucified.
rows.anchor: واختلف في أنهما هل رأيا رؤيا أو لم يريا شيئا فتحالما اختبارا ليوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They asked for interpretations of both dreams and their outcome; plural ‘tell us’ is narrative wording although each man asked separately, like messengers addressed individually.
rows.anchor: وصيغة المتكلم مع الغير واقعة في الحكاية دون المحكي على طريقة قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing Joseph as good may mean they recognized his skill at dream interpretation, whose readings came true, or that he treated prisoners well and could relieve their distress.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون من الرؤية بالعين وأن يكون من الرؤية بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph comforted prisoners who had lost hope and suffered long grief, telling them to be glad, patient, and expect reward.
rows.anchor: وكان في السجن ناس قد انقطع رجاؤهم وطال حزنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The survivor was the cupbearer; ‘remembered’ derives from idh-tadhakkara, with tāʾ changed to dāl and assimilated with dhāl, meaning he recalled Joseph.
rows.anchor: وادكر أصله اذتكر فقلبت التاء دالا والذال دالا وأدغمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘After an ummah’ means after a long period, here seven years; the clause is circumstantial, and the long period resembles a collective of many days and hours.
rows.anchor: بعد أمة أي مدة طويلة حاصلة من اجتماع الأيام الكثيرة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: The king was bewildered by his dream; seeing this, the cupbearer remembered Joseph and his interpretation and offered to bring the answer.
rows.anchor: أي تذكر الناجي يوسف وتأويله رؤياه ورؤيا صاحبه وطلبه أن يذكره عند الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer asked permission to go to prison because Joseph, a wise man of Jacob’s family, had previously interpreted their dreams.
rows.anchor: فأرسلوه إلى يوسف فأتاه فاعتذر إليه وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer calls Joseph truthful because he had tested Joseph’s honesty interpreting both his own dream and his companion’s.
rows.anchor: البليغ في الصدق وإنما وصفه بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king’s singular envoy says ‘advise us’ in the plural because the dream concerned public affairs; he preserves the king’s wording because wording may affect interpretation.
rows.anchor: ففي قوله أفتنا مع أن المستفتي واحد إشعار بأن الرؤيا ليست له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoy hopes the people will learn the interpretation through Joseph.
rows.anchor: لعلي أرجع إلى الناس (تا باشدكه بازكردم بآن جواب تمام بسوى مردمان يعني ملك وملازمان او) لعلهم يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾban is an adverbial verbal noun meaning they should farm continuously and diligently, following their usual practice.
rows.anchor: مصدر دأب في العمل إذا جد فيه وتعب وانتصابه على الحالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harth is sowing seed and preparing soil, while zarʿ is tending and growing the crop; zarʿ is broader because it can also mean sowing, while God causes growth.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الحرث والزرع أن الحرث القاء البذر وتهيئة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph forecast seven abundant years and recommended leaving grain in its ears to protect it from pests; green ears may have suggested this unusual storage method.
rows.anchor: اتركوه فيه ولا تذروه كيلا يأكله السوس كما هو شأن غلال مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should eat only a little during the seven plentiful years and store the rest; Joseph’s instruction teaches restraint and economy.
rows.anchor: مما تأكلون في تلك السنين فأنتم تدرسون وقت حاجتكم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven severe years are famine, harder for people than captivity or killing; their inhabitants consume the grain stored in its ears, expressed figuratively as years eating it.
rows.anchor: سبع سنين صعاب على الناس لأن الجوع أشد من الأسر والقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording hints that the dream’s thin cows did not literally eat the fat cows; the famine years consume stored grain instead.
rows.anchor: وفيه تلويح بأنه تأويل لا كل العجاف السمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is what people preserve as seed for sowing after the famine.
rows.anchor: إلا قليلا مما تحصنون تحرزون وتدخرون للبذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yughāth may mean rain is sent, from the three-letter root ghayth, or people are rescued, from the four-letter root ghawth; the alif reflects the respective root vowel.
rows.anchor: أي يمطرون فيكون بناؤه من ثلاثي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the form may derive from ghawth and mean rescue from hardship.
rows.anchor: فالألف مقلوبة من الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the prosperous year, abundance lets people press grapes, sugarcane, olives, sesame, and similar produce.
rows.anchor: ما شأنه أن يعصر من العنب والقصب والزيتون والسمسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ‘in it’ distinguishes rain and relief, acts of God, from pressing, an act people perform.
rows.anchor: وتكرير فيه لأن الغيث والغوث من فعل الله والعصر من فعل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final year’s glad tidings came by revelation, not from the king’s dream; the cows and ears symbolize fertile years, thin cows and dry ears famine, and stored abundance is consumed.
rows.anchor: وإنما تلقاه من جهة الوحي فبشرهم بها

rows.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
rows.claim: The poem contrasts the lover’s apparent gain and loss and asks for annihilation, abiding, and encounter; the author prays to be among those people.
rows.anchor: عاشق بي مايه را عين زيانست سود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king is Rayyan of Egypt; after the cupbearer returned with Joseph’s interpretation, the king admired his learning and wanted to honor him and hear him directly.
rows.anchor: أي ملك مصر وهو الريان ائتوني به أي بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph told the envoy to return to his master and investigate what happened with the women who cut their hands at Zulaikha’s gathering.
rows.anchor: إرجع إلى ربك أي سيدك فاسأله ليسأل ويتفحص ما بال النسوة اللاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph avoided naming his former mistress out of respect and caution about her schemes; he trusted the other women to admit she solicited him and he resisted.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر سيدته تأدبا ومراعاة لحقها واحترازا عن مكرها

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars say Joseph delayed leaving prison until the king established his innocence, especially before the Aziz, displaying patience and preventing jealous people from defaming him.
rows.anchor: إنما أبى يوسف عليه السلام أن يخرج من السجن إلا بعد أن يتفحص الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His conduct teaches the need to dispel suspicion and avoid places that invite it; a hadith says believers should not enter suspicious situations.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه ينبغي أن يجتهد في نفي التهمة ويتقى مواضعها

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: The king first summoned Joseph only for dream interpretation; after seeing his integrity, patience, resolve, judgment, and restraint, he summoned him again as an intimate.
rows.anchor: كان استدعاء الملك يوسف أولا بسبب علم الرؤيا فلذلك قال ائتوني به فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king calls Joseph trustworthy and high-ranking from that day; ‘today’ marks when these qualities begin, not a later period.
rows.anchor: مكين ذو مكانة ومنزلة رفيعة أمين مؤتمن على كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph left prison after bidding its people farewell and praying for them; the account says news reached the prisoners before the public and records an inscription calling prison a trial-house and grave for the living.
rows.anchor: فخرج من السجن وودع أهل السجن ودعا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph washed, changed into new clothes, and was escorted to the king; al-Taysīr reports seventy chamberlains and seventy mounts were sent to the prison.
rows.anchor: ثم اغتسل وتنظف من درن السجن ولبس ثيابا جددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sufi anecdotes treat fragrance as a spiritual sign beyond ordinary sight: Bayazid sensed Abu al-Hasan al-Kharqani’s coming presence, as the Prophet sensed a divine fragrance from Yemen and Uways al-Qarani.
rows.anchor: همنانكه مصطفى را از يمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fand means senility, impaired reason, and corrupt judgment caused by old age; one calls an old man mufannad, not an old woman, whose poor judgment is not newly caused by age.
rows.anchor: أي تنسبوني إلى الفند وهو الخرف ونقصان العقل وفساد الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspoken result of ‘were it not that you would accuse me’ is that they would believe him; senility does not afflict prophets and spiritual heirs.
rows.anchor: وجواب لولا محذوف تقديره لولا تفنيدكم لصدقتموني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He gulps it’ answers an implied question; the verb conveys forced effort and repeated sips driven by thirst and heat because the drink is bitter and foul.
rows.anchor: وفي التفعل تكلف ومعنى التكلف أن الفاعل يتعانى ذلك الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He can scarcely swallow it and chokes, enduring prolonged torment sip after sip; smooth passage down the throat is what ‘easy to swallow’ means.
rows.anchor: بل يغص به فيشربه باللتيا والتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes the drink scorching the face and making the scalp fall as it nears; when swallowed, it cuts the intestines until they emerge from the anus.
rows.anchor: إنه يقرب إليه فيتكرهه فإذا أدنى منه شوى وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death comes from every direction as the causes of suffering, from all six sides or every part of the body; any one pain would be fatal if death were possible, but the person remains alive.
rows.anchor: ويحيط به من الجهات الست فالمراد بالمكان الجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Behind him’ means ahead of him, after the pus; the next punishment is an ever thicker torment beyond what he has experienced.
rows.anchor: ومن ورائه من بين يديه أي بعد الصديد

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says each succeeding moment brings a more severe punishment, correcting any assumption that torment eases over time.
rows.anchor: عذاب غليظ لا يعرف كنهه أي يستقبل كل وقت عذابا أشد

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl describes the punishment as cutting off breath and confining it in bodies, which explains why crucifixion is among the severest punishments.
rows.anchor: وعن الفضيل هو قطع الأنفاس وحبسها على الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text mentions relief from punishment for Abu Lahab and Abu Talib; Abu Lahab freed his nurse Thuwayba after she announced Muhammad’s birth and receives a little water in Hell on Mondays.
rows.anchor: أول من أرضعته عليه السلام بعد إرضاع أمه له فبشرته بولادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable’s syntax may make the disbelievers’ strange condition the subject and their deeds like ashes its predicate, or leave the predicate implicit and explain it in a new sentence.
rows.anchor: أعمالهم كرماد كقولك صفة زيد عرضه مهتوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind’s ‘intensifying’ means rushing away with the ashes; the day is called stormy by metonymy for its strong wind.
rows.anchor: الاشتداد هنا بمعنى العدو والباء للتعدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection the disbelievers find no reward or mitigation in their good deeds, just as no trace remains of ash scattered by a gale.
rows.anchor: لا يرون له أثرا من ثواب وتخفيف عذاب كما لا يرون أثرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their compounded error is disbelief, ostentation, and pride in deeds they imagine good; unlike sinful believers, they do not repent because they see no fault in themselves.
rows.anchor: وأعمالهم المبنية عليه وعلى التفاخر والرياء مع حسبانهم محسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Charity, kinship, freeing slaves or captives, helping the distressed, and hospitality are nullified when done without knowledge of God, faith, and seeking His face, like ashes blown away.
rows.anchor: شبه الله صنائع الكفار من الصدقة وصلة الرحم وعتق الرقاب وفك الأسير

rows.speaker: الحجاج
rows.claim: Asked about the most pleasing sound, one courtier names Quran recitation at night, another news of a newborn son, and Shuʿba ibn ʿAlqama hearing food served when hungry; al-Hajjaj jokes that Tamim people insist on food.
rows.anchor: ما سمعت صوتا أرق من صوت قارىء حسن الصوت يقرأ كتاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Were people punished for wrongdoing, every creature on earth would perish; animals die at their appointed terms, whereas human destruction is punishment for injustice.
rows.anchor: ما ترك على وجه الأرض من دابة قط بل أهلكها بالكلية بشؤم ظلم الظالمين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra rejects the claim that an oppressor harms only himself: even a bustard dies in its nest because of the oppressor’s wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: حتى أن الحبارى لتموت في وكرها بظلم الظالم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says universal punishment for human sins would reach every creature, even beetles in their holes, and stop rain; God instead delays through forgiveness and grace.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : لو عذب الله الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoing harms outwardly and inwardly: burning one house can spread across a neighborhood or city and kill animals and insects.
rows.anchor: إن أثر الظلم ضار صورة ومعنى وذلك أن أحدا إذا أحرق بيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God delays people with forbearance until a fixed term, whether their lifetimes or punishment, allowing them to multiply or their punishment to increase; when it arrives, they cannot postpone it.
rows.anchor: بحلمه {إلى أجل مسمى} أي : معين لأعمارهم أو لعذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form of ‘seek to delay’ highlights their inability even if they want it; an hour is the briefest interval, and inability to advance emphasizes the impossibility of changing the term.
rows.anchor: وصيغة الاستفعال للاشعار بعجزهم عنه مع طلبهم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers attribute daughters to God, what they hate for themselves, while claiming what they desire; their tongues falsely promise a good afterlife if resurrection is true.
rows.anchor: يثبتون له سبحانه وينسبون إليه في زعمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional claim about a good outcome does not conflict with denying resurrection, since merely supposing resurrection is enough for the condition.
rows.anchor: فلا ينافي قولهم لا يبعث الله من يموت فإنه يكفي في صحته الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘No doubt’ refutes their hope: they get Hell instead of the good they expected; mufraṭūn can mean rushed there or forgotten and left there.
rows.anchor: رد لكلامهم ذلك وإثبات لنقيضه وهو مصدر بمعنى حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preacher challenges a rich man to compare what he gave rulers and attendants with what he gave God, which appears as rags and worthless things at judgment.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم أنه قال لرجل من الأغنياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham dreamt of a warning not to prefer the transient over the lasting or be deceived by power; he woke, repented, and turned to worship, recalling the command to hasten to forgiveness.
rows.anchor: حكي أن إبراهيم بن أدهم سر ذات يوم بمملكته ونعمته ثم نام

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jami’s poem warns against the world’s seductive charm and urges clinging to guidance rather than its deceiving people.
rows.anchor: هركه دل برعشوة كيتى نهاد بر حذر باش از غرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain revives dry earth by producing plants; this figuratively compares growth and freshness with life and dryness with death, without requiring simultaneous events.
rows.anchor: أنبت بسبب المطر في الأرض أنواع النباتات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain and revived earth are signs of God’s unity, knowledge, power, and wisdom, since idols cannot produce them; reflective listeners hear the reminder while others are like the deaf.
rows.anchor: دالة على وحدته تعالى وعلمه وقدرته وحكمته إذ الأصنام وغيرها لا تقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock comprises camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; their milk is a sign carrying people from ignorance to knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهي الأنواع الأربعة التي هي الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says asqā and saqā both mean to give someone drink; another lexicon says asqā grants ongoing watering while saqā gives a single drink.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج سقيته وأسقيته بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘their bellies’ refers either to female livestock, since only they give milk, or to the whole class previously mentioned.
rows.anchor: والضمير يعود إلى بعض الأنعام وهو الإناث لأن اللبن لا يكون للكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ‘from’ marks milk’s origin between the rumen’s residue and blood; the rumen is the animal’s counterpart to a human stomach.
rows.anchor: من ابتدائية متعلقة بنسقيكم لأن بين الفرث والدم مبدأ الإسقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure milk has neither blood’s color nor offal’s smell, and passes easily down the throat; it is said that nobody chokes on it.
rows.anchor: صافيا ليس عليه لون الدم ولا رائحة الفرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report recommends asking blessing over food and milk and says the speaker knows no food or drink more beneficial than milk.
rows.anchor: فإني لا أعلم شيئا أنفع في الطعام والشراب منه

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi describes the stomach separating fodder into residue, milk, and blood; divine power keeps them unmixed, while the liver routes blood to veins, milk to udders, and residue onward.
rows.anchor: خلق الله اللبن في مكان وسط بين الفرث والدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People extract drink and food from dates and grapes; the lexicon defines sukr as wine or date wine.
rows.anchor: السكر محركة الخمر ونبيذ يتخذ من التمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse predates wine’s prohibition and signals disapproval by contrasting intoxicant with good provision, since what opposes good is not good.
rows.anchor: فالآية سابقة على تحريم الخمر دالة على كراهتها حيث قوبل السكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good provision includes dates, syrup, raisins, date paste, and vinegar; a report calls vinegar the best condiment, and al-Maʾmun recounts using wine vinegar for cough.
rows.anchor: كالتمر والدبس والزبيب والرب والخل وفي الحديث "خير خلكم خل خمركم"

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The wording distinguishes gifts requiring no human processing, for which God says ‘We give you drink,’ from products people must prepare, for which it says ‘you make.’
rows.anchor: لما كان اللبن لا يحتاج إلى معالجة من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These products are a clear sign for people who use reason to consider the evidence.
rows.anchor: يستعملون عقولهم في الآيات بالنظر والتأمل

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, dates are fruits of obedience and grapes fruits of spiritual struggle; their yield includes mystical unveilings, visions, and seekers’ extraordinary states.
rows.anchor: ومن ثمرات نخيل الطاعات وأعناب المجاهدات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The ego drinks intoxicating products of spiritual effort and veers from the straight path or displays vanity; heart and spirit receive provision that increases longing, love, sincerity, and seeking.
rows.anchor: السكر ما يجعل منها شرب النفس فتسكر النفس فتارة تميل عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bee inspiration resembles guidance for spiritual travelers: they withdraw to mountains like the Prophet’s retreats at Hira, maintain cleanliness, and avoid polluted places and foods.
rows.anchor: خص النحل بالوحي وهو الإلهام والرشد من بين سائر الحيوانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruits of the body are righteous deeds, of the soul ascetic discipline and struggle against desire, of the heart renouncing the world for God, and of the secret witnessing truth and drawing near.
rows.anchor: وثمرات البدن الأعمال الصالحة وثمرات النفوس الرياضات والمجاهدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command to bees to eat all fruits parallels the command to believers to eat wholesome things and act righteously.
rows.anchor: كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes people at different ages, and neither young nor old can advance or delay the appointed term.
rows.anchor: أي : يقبض أرواحكم على اختلاف الأسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some are returned to the most decrepit age, where old age and senility weaken body, reason, and understanding; there is no fixed threshold.
rows.anchor: وليس له حد معلوم في الحقيقة لأنه رب ابن ستين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says reaching ninety can end one’s ability to work, manage affairs, earn, perform pilgrimage, or campaign.
rows.anchor: إذا بلغ تسعين سنة يتعطل عن العمل والتصرف والاكتساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows lifespan measures and can take a vigorous youth or preserve a worn elder; unequal timing reflects wise divine determination rather than natural necessity.
rows.anchor: قدير على كل شيء يميت الشاب النشيط ويبقى الهرم الفاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life is divided into seven stages: childhood to seven, boyhood to fourteen, youth to thirty-two, then middle age and old age through life’s end.
rows.anchor: طور الطفولية إلى سبع سنين

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad groups life into growth, stable youth, mild decline in middle age, and severe decline in old age; senility is worst because it mimics childhood and has no cure.
rows.anchor: والثانية سن الوقوف وهي سن الشباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from miserliness, laziness, decrepit age, grave punishment, the Antichrist’s trial, and the trials of life and death.
rows.anchor: وأرذل العمر وعذاب القبر وفتنة الدجال وفتنة المحيا والممات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say decrepitude applies to disbelievers, while a Muslim’s reason grows with age through piety; a hadith says Quran reciters are not returned to decrepit age, as are those who reflect and act on it.
rows.anchor: حكم الهرم إنما يظهر في حق الكافر لأن المسلم يزداد عقله لصلاحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that scholars escape dementia applies to scholars of the afterlife and those who know God, not all scholars; the author has seen contemporaries regress to childishness.
rows.anchor: علماء الآخرة والعلماء بالله لا مطلق العلماء كما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though decrepit age is hard, it is also a time for forgiveness and higher rank; a report says good deeds are confirmed at eighty and sins erased.
rows.anchor: لكنه أوان المغفرة ورفعة الدرجة وفي الحديث

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The chained hand and the fully outstretched hand are twin images warning against stinginess and extravagance and urging the middle course of generosity.
rows.anchor: هما تمثيلان لمنع الشحيح وإعطاء المسرف زجرا لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not withhold rightful spending until unable to give, nor give away everything until nothing remains; either extreme leaves a person blamed or destitute.
rows.anchor: ولا تمسك يدك عن النفقة في الحق كل الإمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two prohibitions govern ‘you become’; blame before God and people follows withholding, while regret or depletion follows total spending.
rows.anchor: جواب للنهيين أي : فتصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Persian poem praises the balanced middle path across all affairs as the best course.
rows.anchor: بدان دليل كه خير الأمور أوسطها

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi says the address is to the Prophet though intended for others, since he was so open-handed he saved nothing for the next day.
rows.anchor: الصحيح أن هذا خطاب للنبي والمراد غيره لأنه أفسح الناس صدرا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi recounts a Muslim-Jewish wager that Muhammad was more generous than Moses, then a mother’s request for his shirt; he gave it to her daughter and missed prayer while left unclothed, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در اسباب نزول آمده كه مسلمه

rows.speaker: برهان القرآن
rows.claim: A report says prayer time came while the Prophet was embarrassed to emerge unclothed; companions entered, saw him, and blamed him, so ‘blamed and exposed’ is read literally.
rows.anchor: فدخل وقت الصلاة ولم يخرج للصلاة حياء فدخل عليه أصحابه

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad rejects that report because the sura is Meccan while the incident occurred in Medina; the author leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: ولم يرض في الإرشاد بهذه الرواية بناء على أن السورة مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands or constricts provision for different people according to His will and wisdom.
rows.anchor: يوسعه على بعض ويضيقه على بعض آخرين بمشيئته التابعة للحكمة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, the verse points to leaving human and natural inclinations for servanthood through trust and surrender; God alternates expansion and constriction of the self to regulate its states.
rows.anchor: يشير به إلى الخروج عن أوطان البشرية والطبيعية الإنسانية إلى قضاء العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred report from Anas says some believers’ faith is sound only with wealth, poverty, health, or illness; God manages them by knowing their hearts.
rows.anchor: رواه أنس رضي الله عنه كما في "بحر العلوم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith urges hastening to good works before tempting wealth, forgetfulness-inducing poverty, senility, corrupting illness, and sudden death.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "بادروا بالأعمال خمسا : غنى مطغيا وفقرا منسيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening ‘when’ can function as an adverb modifying ‘wonder’ or as the object of ‘remember’; it means they went to and took refuge in the cave.
rows.anchor: ظرف لعجبا أو مفعول لأذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths were noble Romans who refused Daqyanus’s coercion to worship idols and fled to a cave in their mountain.
rows.anchor: فتية من أشراف الروم أكرههم دقيانوس على الشرك فأبوا وهربوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitya means vigorous young men and can metaphorically describe rulers even when old; a prophetic report prefers ‘my young man’ over ‘my slave,’ while Abu Yusuf says the term admits bondage.
rows.anchor: والفتية جمع الفتى وهو الشاب القوي الحدث ويستعار للملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘From Your presence’ means from the hidden treasuries of special mercy, inaccessible to hostile eyes; they ask mercy bringing forgiveness, provision, and safety from enemies.
rows.anchor: من خزائن رحمتك الخاصة المكنونة عن عيون أهل المعاداة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both prepositional phrases attach to ‘prepare’; preparation means ordering their migration from unbelievers and perseverance in obedience, while rushd is the path to the goal.
rows.anchor: هيأت الشيء أصلحته والإصلاح نقيض الإفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Striking their ears is a metaphor for placing a barrier against hearing: deep sleep resembles a curtain over the ears, singled out because they usually wake a solitary sleeper.
rows.anchor: حجابا يمنع سماعها أي : أنمناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to their prayer included sleep and the subsequent turning from side to side, a hidden grace beyond ordinary causal means.
rows.anchor: وما ترتب عليه من التقليب ذات اليمين وذات الشمال وغير ذلك ايتاء رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave is the place of sleep and ‘years’ its duration; the 309 years are called numbered either to magnify divine power or make the duration seem small beside God’s timeless measure.
rows.anchor: ذوات عدد هي ثلاثمائة وتسع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God awakened them from heavy sleep resembling death, showing that sleep shares death’s suspension of life and is followed by resurrection.
rows.anchor: أيقظناهم من تلك النومة الثقيلة الشبيهة بالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That We may know’ means testing, named by its result; such a test need not produce the tested action and can expose inability, as in the command to bring the sun from the west.
rows.anchor: العلم هنا مجاز عن الاختبار بطريق إطلاق اسم المسبب على السبب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the two parties as the youths and the successive kings who ruled their city.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن أحد الحزبين الفتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks which group best counted the stay; ahṣā is past tense meaning counted, not a comparative, and amad means duration or endpoint.
rows.anchor: فأحصى فعل ماض هنا وهو الصحيح لا أفعل تفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test shows both parties’ inability to count, leading them to entrust the matter to God, recognize His preservation of bodies and faith, and gain certainty in His power, knowledge, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: فيزدادوا يقينا بكمال قدرته وعلمه ويستبصروا به أمر البعث

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says retreating seekers are more astonishing: their cave is the retreat cell, their hearts bear the inscription of love and divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: في أمتك من هو أعجب حالا منهم وذلك أن فيهم أصحاب الخلوات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The cave youths fled Daqyanus, while seekers in retreat long for encounter with God; they seek rescue from the self and escape from existence’s darkness into divine beauty and majesty.
rows.anchor: آووا إلى كهف الخلوة شوقا إلى لقائي وفرارا إلي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: For retreat seekers, shutting the ears blocks human speech from engraving their hearts and withdraws the senses from imprinting them.
rows.anchor: سد آذان ظاهر أصحاب الخلوة وآذان باطنهم لئلا يقرع مسامعهم كلام الخلق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: They erase prior impressions by constantly repeating ‘There is no god but God’; negation and affirmation purify and illuminate their hearts with divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: يمحون النقوش السابقة عن القلوب بملازمة استعمال كلمة الطلاسة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God manifests His essence and attributes to their hearts, annihilating them from themselves and preserving them through Him.
rows.anchor: يتجلى تبارك وتعالى لقلوبهم بذاته وجميع صفاته فيفنيهم الله عنهم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: ‘Then We raised them’ means God gave them life through Him; the two parties are cave dwellers and retreat seekers, each asking which correctly measured its stay.
rows.anchor: وهو سر قوله : {ثم بعثناهم} أي : أحييناهم بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We narrate’ means explain their story; ‘in truth’ qualifies an omitted verbal noun, since storytellers distort accounts to suit their temper and desire, and only God narrates truly.
rows.anchor: نقص قصا ملتبسا بالحق والصدق

rows.speaker: التكملة
rows.claim: A disciple of Jesus refused to bow at the city idol, worked in a nearby bath, and taught local youths until they believed; after the king’s son and a woman died in the bath, the disciple fled and the youths escaped to the cave.
rows.anchor: قال في "التكملة" : سبب إيمانهم أن حواريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author thinks they were moved to faith by heavenly inspiration and divine attraction without an evidentiary argument, as the Najmiyya commentary suggests.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن إيمانهم كان بالإلهام الملكوتي والانجذاب اللاهوتي

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some say they lived before Jesus, who told people their story, and awoke after his ascension during the interval before Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فروى بعض الناس أنهم كانوا قبل عيسى ابن مريم وأن عيسى أخبر قومه

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Another account places them after Jesus as Christians; al-Tabari says this is the view of most scholars.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري وعليه أكثر العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increased their guidance by establishing them firmly in true religion and revealing its hidden beauties.
rows.anchor: بأن ثبتناهم على الدين الحق وأظهرنا لهم مكنونات محاسنه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: They are called fityan because their faith was verified rather than imitated; they sought guidance from God through God, initially within their own understanding and capacity.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : سماهم باسم الفتوة لأنهم آمنوا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God exceeded their hoped-for guidance: after 309 years they awoke with bodies and clothes unchanged, so faith became certainty and the unseen became direct vision.
rows.anchor: بعد ثلاثمائة وتسع سنين وما تغيرت أحوالهم وما بليت ثيابهم
